_provenance.description: Stan ADVI and Turing.jl ADVI SVI arms added to the three continuous PPLBench models (logistic_regression, robust_regression, n_schools) under the same SVI PPLBench protocol as svi_pplbench_results_2026-07-13b.json. This file adds the 'Stan' and 'Turing.jl' frameworks; the 'NumPyro' and 'Impulse' entries are copied verbatim from svi_pplbench_results_2026-07-13b.json for side-by-side comparison (marked _source='reference ...').
_provenance.protocol: PPLBench trials-as-chains SVI: iterations=200 (K=200 posterior draws from the fitted mean-field guide), num_warmup=0, 4 trials. overall n_eff = arviz.ess over all latent params with the 4 trials as 4 chains; n_eff/s median = overall n_eff median / steady-state (trials 1..3) fit wall time; PLL = per-trial final cumulative predictive log-likelihood on the held-out test items using the K=200 guide draws. Only the guide FIT is timed as the inference phase; compile/startup recorded separately. Data identical to the standard configs (seed 12345): logistic n=10000 k=10 rho=3.0; robust n=10000 k=10; n_schools n=10000.

Turing.jl.algorithm: AdvancedVI KLMinRepGradDescent (the ADVI alias in AdvancedVI 0.6.2), reparameterization-gradient ELBO
Turing.jl.guide_init: unconstrained location = 0, diagonal scale = init_scale = 0.1 (matches the Impulse/NumPyro init)
Turing.jl.optimizer: Optimisers.Adam(lr=step_size=0.01)  -- MATCHES the Impulse/NumPyro Adam lr=0.01
Turing.jl.averager: NoAveraging (return the LAST iterate, matching Adam's final params; not a Polyak average)
Turing.jl.operator: ClipScale (AdvancedVI's recommended singular-scale safeguard for MvLocationScale; not an optimizer change)
Turing.jl.adtype: AutoForwardDiff() -- the ONLY AD backend in turing_env; no ReverseDiff/Mooncake/Zygote installed, so forward-mode over the full likelihood (this is why per-trial wall times are large, esp. robust/n_schools)
Turing.jl.draws: after the fit, K=200 samples drawn from q.dist (unconstrained MvLocationScale), then DynamicPPL.unflatten(linked VarInfo) + invlink back to constrained space, read per named site -> same site layout as the Turing NUTS extractor
Turing.jl.package_versions: Turing 0.42.9, AdvancedVI 0.6.2, DynamicPPL 0.39.15, Bijectors 0.15.16, ForwardDiff 1.3.2 (turing_env, unchanged)
Turing.jl.note: Old-style `vi(model, ADVI(1,2000))` and DecayedADAGrad no longer exist in this Turing/AdvancedVI; KLMinRepGradDescent(adtype; optimizer=Adam, n_samples, averager, operator) is the equivalent and lets Adam lr=0.01 be passed cleanly, so the Turing arm's optimizer MATCHES the Impulse/NumPyro protocol exactly (unlike Stan).

Stan.algorithm: CmdStan variational (ADVI), algorithm=meanfield, via cmdstanpy 1.3.0 CmdStanModel.variational
Stan.guide: Stan ADVI mean-field Gaussian in the unconstrained space (== AutoNormal mean-field)
Stan.optimizer: Stan's OWN adaptive stochastic optimizer: automatic eta (step-size) adaptation followed by adaptive-stepsize SGD with a relative-ELBO convergence test (tol_rel_obj default 0.01). CANNOT be pinned to Adam lr=0.01 / 2000 steps like the other three arms; runs Stan defaults for eta/iter/tol_rel_obj (iter default 10000 max with early stopping). This is the documented protocol deviation for the Stan arm.
Stan.output_samples: 200 (K post-fit draws, exposed via --output-samples -> cmdstanpy draws=200)
Stan.require_converged: False (harness robustness: return the fitted approximation even when Stan's own heuristic flags non-convergence, rather than crashing the arm). Stan's convergence flag is recorded per model below.
Stan.draws: cmdstanpy CmdStanVB.stan_variables(mean=False) -> per-draw constrained samples, leading axis = 200, fed unchanged through the existing extract_data_from_stan pipeline
Stan.package_versions: cmdstanpy 1.3.0 (probprog-bench env), CmdStan toolchain as used by the Stan MCMC arm

_provenance.commands: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' ./run_pplbench.sh --device cpu --threads 32 --ppls <turing|stan> svi/<model>  (run from benchmark/probprog). Each arm run separately for clean per-trial timing.
_provenance.env: CPU only (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''), 32 threads. Stan via probprog-bench python; Turing via turing_env (unchanged Project.toml). No native rebuild.
files_added_or_modified: stan_harness.py (added --method svi VI path: run_vi_trial/vi_main/_vi_write_diagnostics + argparse args; MCMC run_trial/write_output/main NUTS path unchanged)
turing_harness.jl (added --method svi ADVI path: run_turing_advi/svi_draw_and_extract/svi_main + argparse args + branch; NUTS run_turing_nuts/extract_samples path unchanged)
pplbench_configs/svi/{logistic_regression,robust_regression,n_schools}.json (added non-optional stan + turing ppl blocks: legend Stan/green, Turing.jl/purple)

svi/logistic_regression.Turing.jl: OK (in band). PLL_final_mean -75.96 vs NumPyro -71.55 / Impulse -72.13. final_elbo mean -123.2 (ref NumPyro -114.4 / Impulse -122.6). Converged (ELBO -260@200 -> -170@800 -> -117..-130@2000); site means match NumPyro. Slightly worse optimum from Turing's Adam dynamics + forward-mode AD, not a bug.
svi/logistic_regression.Stan: FAILED TO CONVERGE (divergent). Stan's own ADVI heuristic printed 'The algorithm may not have converged' on ALL 4 trials. Posterior means diverge: alpha pooled -19.28 (per-trial -31.9/-8.3/-28.5/-8.4) vs NumPyro -1.62; |beta| up to 8.0 vs NumPyro ~0.3-0.66; alpha std 11.0 vs 0.155. pll_final_mean -42.52 is numerically 'high' only because a few saturated draws dominate the logsumexp; the posterior is not usable. Diagnosis: known Stan ADVI instability on wide-prior (alpha_scale=10) + correlated (rho=3) logistic regression; NOT a harness bug -- the SAME harness/extract path converges correctly on robust and n_schools (below). n_eff median 5.5 reflects the large across-seed disagreement.

svi/robust_regression.Turing.jl: OK (in band). PLL_final_mean -7243.16 vs NumPyro -7212.84 / Impulse -7211.06 (NumPyro's own trials spanned -7202..-7218). Per-site means MATCH NumPyro to 3-4 digits: alpha -14.234 vs -14.231, nu 7.98 vs 8.08, sigma 0.994 vs 0.939, all 10 betas identical. Positive-support (nu Gamma, sigma Exponential) transforms correct. final_elbo ~-7540 (ref -7446/-7461). Converged to essentially the same posterior means; tiny PLL gap is trial noise.
svi/robust_regression.Stan: Converged (no Stan convergence warning). PLL_final_mean -7365.77 vs -7212.84, ~150 worse (per-trial -7334/-7398/-7329/-7402). Per-site: alpha -14.234 vs -14.231 and all betas MATCH; but nu 41.5 vs 8.08 (Stan ADVI mean-field pushes the Student-t dof high -> near-Gaussian tails) and sigma 1.07 vs 0.94. So Stan converged to a worse-fitting but stable optimum (heavier reliance on sigma, inflated nu); a genuine optimizer/family difference, not a bug (means + layout correct).

svi/n_schools.Turing.jl: OK (in band, slightly BETTER). PLL_final_mean -6878.16 vs NumPyro -6886.01 / Impulse -6889.17. final_elbo -7060 (ref -7120/-7085). Positive HalfCauchy sigma sites correctly recovered via DynamicPPL invlink (no column-order collapse -- the extractor keys by site name, so the Impulse-harness declaration-vs-alphabetical bug cannot occur here).
svi/n_schools.Stan: OK (in band). PLL_final_mean -6889.06 vs -6886.01 (per-trial -6892.8/-6888.4/-6892.0/-6883.1). No Stan convergence warning. Positive sigma sites recovered (sigma_state ~3.3, sigma_district ~2.2, sigma_type ~3.1, beta_baseline ~-3.9); close to NumPyro means, expected ADVI-optimizer offset.
